Ad tech is killing the online experience

Very irritating ≠ "killing the online experience". Those are two different things. People aren't going to stop using the web. They're going to stop visiting the sites that are the most annoying to them.

The funny thing about ads is I don't mind them unless they are popping up in my face and breaking my focus from what I came to a site for. I use adblock because the internet is pretty much unusable without it. If they learned that a simple banner ad was enough, it wouldn't be necessary to use the blocker.
Another thing that grinds my gears about ads is how many of them there are. I read something a week or two ago that stated that a college started using adblock on all of their computers, and that reduced bandwidth consumption by 40%. Not only are these unwanted ads popping up and ruining our online experience, they are costing us time and money.

For the last several years I've been a member of Google Adsense- I've used their service to put banner ads on my websites; I started with my little book review blog and eventually put them on my gaming site. I've still not made $100 from them.

I've worked very hard on these sites as a writer; I don't regret the time I've spent, and I don't regret having unobtrusive ads. That said, I do wish ad revenue wasn't worth mere pennies. The low value of ads disincentivizes the production of high quality articles. Why work 3-4 weeks on an in-depth examination of a game genre when I can race the other sites to be the first with screenshots or something equally lame and pull in monster hits for it?

The need to post ordinary stuff hasn't stopped me from making cool stuff, but it has slowed me down significantly.
So basically you are saying its a lose-lose situation?

Which is why I actually kind of like the "allow some ads" idea of adblock. I strongly agree it should be an option for the user to decide, but we should be encouraging the use of non-intrusive ads over intrusive ones. If we could get to the point that non-intrusive ads were generating more money than intrusive ones, websites would start to cut back.
The worst thing about ads is the amount of malware distributed by them.

If they learned that a simple banner ad was enough, it wouldn't be necessary to use the blocker.

It's not just advertisers who violate this, but the sites themselves as well. They have to code in where the ads will go, so at some level there's a partnership between the people providing the content and the people providing the ads. If websites weren't trying to sell so much adspace on their sites then they might restrict themselves to only a banner advertisement.

Of course that then begs the question of why do they feel the need to increase the number of ads running on their pages? Is it simple greed, or are they unable to make their operating costs otherwise? I'm sure the answer to that question depends on the site, but there's easily a lot more going on than just "advertisers are evil and trying to sell ads nonstop."
I haven't seen online ads in about 12 years.
Haven't seen them or haven't noticed them?

I also find it interesting how Google has sort of sparked things to get this out of control. Back in the day (before Google infiltrated our lives) the web was a complete mess with horrible flashing Ads plastered all over the damn place on every page; it was literally a task in itself to close popups and try to figure out what on the page was actual content and where the ads ended. Then Google stepped in and said - hey, we give you great search results to what you actually want, and we do it with a nice, clean interface: plain white background, the word "Google" and a text input box with a search button next to it (and maybe the "feeling lucky thing"). And everyone rejoiced and said - holy shit the web can be clean and aesthetically pleasing AND be functional. And now it's almost like we're right back where we fucking were and I feel like I'm using Lycos in 1998 through an AOL client. The arguments I hear are "well they need to pay the bills" which is true - but if you plaster your site in ads and push your user base away you're doing more harm than good. Then everyone either leaves or starts blacklisting you with Ad-blockers and you lose out anyway.
